direction: Refine the scale-normalized generalized savings merge score with the balanced-fill variant (lam≈1.08, mu≈0.12, beta_fill≈0.10, beta_balance≈0.05) and let EoH co-evolve the four dimensionless coefficients (lam, mu, beta_fill, beta_balance, plus scale divisor choice) rather than hard-coding, keeping the one-shot vectorized evaluation to preserve the sub-4ms p95 at the 25ms budget.

operations.mechanism: Diagnostic on dev_24 at 25ms with the generalization of the KB L2a rule (global depot-distance normalization, lam=1.08, mu=0.12) plus a dimensionless capacity-fill reward (0.10) and a new endpoint demand-balance reward (0.05) gives mean 16.1205 vs the round-1 archive SBS 16.1921 (-0.44%), with 24/24 completed, 0 exhausted, p50 2.19ms / p95 3.34ms — i.e. ~13% of the 25ms budget, leaving large headroom. Weak regimes remain size=100 (20.84), eccentric depot (19.32), tight capacity (18.56), so more merge-order fidelity (edge-weight lam, radial asymmetry mu) is still worth harvesting. Since the hook is a one-shot vectorized scoring pass, extra coefficient degrees of freedom cost no runtime, so submitting the balanced-fill family for inner EoH evolution is a risk-free improvement direction.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: Adding a dimensionless endpoint demand-balance term (1 - |q_i-q_j|/(q_i+q_j)) on top of the scale-normalized generalized savings + capacity-fill score strictly improves dev_24 mean tour length relative to pure fill-weighted savings (16.1921), because it reduces tail-fragment routes by pairing comparable-demand endpoints; and EoH perturbing lam in [1.00,1.20], mu in [0.05,0.20], beta_fill in [0.0,0.20], beta_balance in [0.0,0.12] will find a strictly better static merge rule without any budget-exhaustion risk (p95 stays <5ms of 25ms).
